messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate detected for /v1/generate from cluster inference-prod. 5xx rate spike to 4.8% in last 5m. Affected pods: worker-45, worker-47. Error signature: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS.

alice-ops: I'm seeing runtime crashes on worker-45. kubectl logs shows repeated: 
```
E tensorflow: 2026-02-10 14:12:01.123456 CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS: misaligned address during pagewalk
stack: runtime_kernel.cu:0x7ff...
```
Will collect full logs. Paging thrash reported during heavy batching.

ben-sre: copying dmesg from node gpu-12 (attached): 
```
[Feb10 14:11:59] nvmap: pagewalk: misaligned PTE at 0x7f8a2c4b0000
[Feb10 14:12:00] BUG: unable to handle kernel paging request at address 0x7f8a2c4b0008
[Feb10 14:12:00] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, PID=9876, GPU reported illegal address
```
Looks like kernel-level pagewalk/translation mismatch. Suspect a driver or kernel NVLink interaction.

luis-runtime: confirmed same segfault in runtime container: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` after nvrtc kernel launch. Repro is intermittent under long-sequence generation with KV cache > 1.5GB. Attaching minimal stack trace and /proc/<pid>/maps.

carmen-ml: tagging possible model vector size buildup. Could be KV cache growth + continuous batching pushing beyond page boundary alignment for some kernels. Any recent runtime image/kernel/driver changes?

alice-ops: deploy-bot reports a runtime image push 3h ago: `runtime:v1.8.0-optim` to inference-prod. Rolling back is candidate mitigation.

eva-support: customer-impact: 3 customers reported 500s in last 10m (IDs: cust-42, cust-88, cust-212). SLA alerts triggered for two. Notified account leads.

ben-sre: mitigation plan (short):
1) Remove worker-45 & 47 from service (cordon + drain)
2) Roll traffic to pool without v1.8.0-optim (fallback to v1.7.3)
3) Collect full coredumps and dmesg + nvml logs, open support ticket with NVIDIA if kernel driver suspicious
4) If rollback reduces errors -> keep rollback and investigate differences between images

alice-ops: executing (1) now: `kubectl cordon worker-45 && kubectl drain worker-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

deploy-bot: rollback triggered: routing 60% traffic off nodes with runtime:v1.8.0-optim -> target image runtime:v1.7.3-stable.

luis-runtime: while draining, attach these debug commands (please run on node with crash):
```
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/gpu-dmesg.log
sudo journalctl -u runtime.service -o short-precise --no-pager > /tmp/runtime-journal.log
sudo coredumpctl dump --output=/tmp/coredump_$(date +%s).core --pid=9876
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,CEC > /tmp/nvml_quick.txt
```
Get file links in #eng-runtime-logs.

carmen-ml: quick repro suggestion: disable batching (set BATCH_SIZE=1) on a canary and try long sequence to exercise KV cache alignment. If it reproduces, we can root cause kernel vs. runtime memory layout.

alice-ops: rollback appears to be reducing errors. Error rate down to 1.2% after 3m. Still seeing a couple of post-rollback 5xxs from worker-47 (which wasn't fully drained). Continuing.

ben-sre: ran `sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 10` on node before drain; got sample showing pagewalk in GPU MMU routine. Attaching sampling summary to thread.

luis-runtime: we captured a core and runtime stack. Key frame points at our kernel launch wrapper -> then a GPU page fault raised by NV driver. Attaching sanitized trace: 
```
#0  0x7f8a2c4b0008 in gpu_pagewalk_fault+0x34 (nv_kern.c)
#1  0x7ffb12ab in cuLaunchKernel
#2  0x400b2c in run_inference (runtime.cu)
#3  0x7fff.. in python run
```
Suggest enabling CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 on a canary to see exact failing kernel and reduce noise.

eva-support: customer updates sent: cust-42 on call now, cust-88 emailed. Will provide ETA as we reduce error rate.

carmen-ml: question: any missing host kernel patch in nodes? Did cloud infra push a kernel update recently?

alice-ops: no kernel updates in last 24h. Only runtime image change and a platform config tweak for hugepage accounting that landed 4h ago: `enable_hugepage_adjust=true` (feature flag). I'm disabling that flag on the node group as an experiment.

ben-sre: disabling hugepage accounting rolled back on node group. Early signal: error rate dropped to 0.3% and worker-47 stabilized. That suggests interaction with hugepages + driver.

luis-runtime: creating a safe hotfix: build runtime:v1.8.0-optim-nohp with hugepage allocation disabled for our CUDA allocator (env REDWOOD_ALLOC_USE_HUGEPAGES=0). Will test on a small canary pool.

alice-ops: canary deployed (5 pods) with runtime:v1.8.0-optim-nohp and REDWOOD_ALLOC_USE_HUGEPAGES=0. Running synthetic load (batch sizes 8-16, long sequences).

deploy-bot: canary metrics after 12m: no CUDA_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS observed. Traffic and latencies nominal.

carmen-ml: good sign. We should avoid full rollback if hotfix works; rollback affects throughput/cost. Plan: patch node group flag + rollout v1.8.0-optim-nohp across affected pool.

eva-support: update to customers: we have a mitigation; some traffic was rerouted temporarily. ETA for full restore: 45m.

ben-sre: filing NVIDIA ticket with NV driver logs + dmesg + core. Case ID: NV-INC-20260210-001. Attached sample workloads and stack traces. Please add any additional traces to NV case.

luis-runtime: also adding reproducer harness to the ticket: small script that runs long-sequence generation loops with KV cache persistence and continuous batching. Reproducer pinned to the same model and token lengths as production.

alice-ops: rolling hotfix to remaining nodes in batches of 10. Using rollout strategy: drain -> update node group flag -> uncordon. Monitoring 5xx rate.

ben-sre: midway update: after 3 batches, global 5xx rate is 0.08%. Two remaining nodes being updated.

carmen-ml: tracking hypothesis: hugepage-backed allocations cause occasional misalignment when combined with our custom KV cache allocator on certain GPU driver versions. Hotfix disables hugepage usage which aligns allocations to safe boundaries. Long-term fix: coordinate with NV driver and possibly update our allocator to ensure page-aligned GPU mappings.

eva-support: customers alerted: cust-42 and cust-88 acknowledged. No data loss, only transient errors.

alice-ops: final nodes updated. Post-rollout metrics: 5xx rate back to baseline 0.02%. CPU/GPU utilization normal. Restoring normal traffic patterns.

luis-runtime: marking incident as mitigated. Captured artifacts: /logs/2315001111/{dmesg,nvml_q.txt,coredump_*.core,perf.data}. NV ticket NV-INC-20260210-001 open.

ben-sre: assigning postmortem to eng-runtime. Primary action items: (a) add guard in allocator for page alignment (b) test matrix across driver/kernel versions + hugepage toggles (c) add alerting for GPU pagewalk faults earlier.

alice-ops: handoff to oncall tomorrow (ben-sre). Please ensure postmortem draft by EOD + include timeline and customer impact numbers.

eva-support: I'll follow up with account teams and push a short customer-facing incident note once postmortem is ready.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: service error rate returned to baseline. Incident status -> mitigated.

ben-sre: noted. Filing follow-up tasks in our incident tracker. Thanks everyone for rapid coordination. :thumbsup:
